_meta.blindness: written from the attacker's external view of HTTP only; NO ONYX detection file was opened while writing this (see _catalog_started_at.txt). Forms are chosen to include shapes the tool was NOT built on (GT3 generalization).
_meta.rule: each class lists the conserved principle it breaks and what an attacker observes on the wire — never how any tool detects it.

classes.principle_broken: an object belongs to a principal; only that principal (or an authorized role) may read/affect it
classes.attacker_observable: request an object id that belongs to another user; the server returns that other user's object data instead of 403/404

forms.name: sequential id swap
forms.how: GET /api/users/{id}/profile with another user's numeric id returns their profile

forms.name: ownership via nested body reference
forms.how: POST /api/transfer with {from_account: <victim_account_uuid>} executes against the victim's account though the path looks self-scoped

forms.name: ownership via secondary key
forms.how: GET /api/orders?invoice=<victim_invoice_code> returns the victim's order; the owning key is a query param, not a path id

classes.principle_broken: a function/action is gated to a role; a principal without the role may not invoke it
classes.attacker_observable: a lower-privilege principal invokes an admin/elevated action (different verb or endpoint) and it executes (2xx + state change) instead of 403

forms.name: method escalation
forms.how: a normal user sends DELETE /api/posts/{id} on a post they do not own and it succeeds

forms.name: shadow admin endpoint
forms.how: a normal user POSTs /api/internal/users/{id}/role {role:'admin'} — the admin path is not linked anywhere but is reachable and executes

forms.name: verb-tunneled action
forms.how: action smuggled via X-HTTP-Method-Override: DELETE on a POST request bypasses the function gate

classes.owasp: API3:2023 Broken Object Property Level Authorization
classes.principle_broken: within an object, specific properties are readable/writable only by authorized principals (excessive data exposure + mass assignment)
classes.attacker_observable: READ: a principal receives a property the server should hide from them (it appears for an admin/owner but is also returned to them in some view). WRITE: a principal sets a protected property via mass-assignment and the server accepts it

forms.name: excessive field in detail view
forms.how: GET on an object returns a sensitive field (e.g. credit balance) to a non-owner that the list view hides

forms.name: inconsistent projection across representations
forms.how: the summary endpoint hides the field but ?expand=full or a sibling endpoint leaks it for the same non-owner

forms.name: mass-assignment privilege write
forms.how: PATCH /api/me {is_admin:true} or {wallet_balance:99999} is silently accepted and reflected on re-read

classes.principle_broken: an endpoint that exposes private data must require a valid principal; anonymous access must be denied
classes.attacker_observable: remove the token entirely (anonymous) and a private resource still returns 2xx with data instead of 401

forms.name: missing auth on private GET
forms.how: GET /api/users/{id}/private with no Authorization header returns data

forms.name: auth required on one method only
forms.how: GET requires auth but HEAD/OPTIONS or a cached variant leaks the same data unauthenticated

decoys._purpose: legitimate differences that MUST be abstained on; an alert here is a false positive = measured precision loss

items.name: feature_flag_same_role
items.how: two same-role users differ on a beta field driven by an A/B flag, not authorization

items.name: null_not_forbidden
items.how: a field is absent for a user simply because it has no value, not because it is withheld

items.name: plan_tier_legit
items.how: a 'premium' field differs by subscription tier the user legitimately holds — a declared, correct difference

items.name: not_found_vs_forbidden
items.how: 404 for a non-existent object (no ownership claim) must never be read as a denial-of-access signal

items.name: correct_owner_denial
items.how: a non-owner correctly receiving 403 — the right behavior, must not be flagged
